title: How International Relations Evolved: Theories and Models

scenes.text: Why do countries prepare for war instead of trusting permanent peace?
scenes.narration: Have you ever wondered why countries spend fortunes on weapons instead of trusting each other? In 1914, scholars launched International Relations to find theories that avoid wars and establish peace.

scenes.text: A housing society without guards where residents buy bigger locks out of fear.
scenes.narration: As an everyday analogy, imagine a housing society without any security guard. Because no authority protects you, you buy extra locks, which panics your neighbours into buying even bigger locks.

scenes.heading: Milestones in World Order

events.what: First university chair of International Politics
League of Nations founded after war
United Nations created for global peace

scenes.narration: That is how international politics worked after the 1648 Treaty of Westphalia created sovereign nation-states. When balance of power failed, devastating world wars prompted leaders to establish the League of Nations and the United Nations.

scenes.heading: The Security Dilemma
scenes.narration: In global politics, anarchy means there is simply no world government. Under this anarchy, countries rely on self-help, arming themselves for safety and accidentally trapping everyone in a security dilemma.

scenes.name: Woodrow Wilson
scenes.idea: Replace balance of power with collective security to establish lasting peace.
scenes.narration: Here is the big debate: idealists like Woodrow Wilson wanted collective security to preserve peace. But realist scholars like E.H. Carr argued that power politics and national interest always dominate.

scenes.heading: Billiard Ball vs Cobweb Model
scenes.narration: Thinkers long viewed states as hard billiard balls constantly colliding in conflict. Today, globalisation has built a cobweb model, connecting citizens and organisations through multiple gateways across the globe.

items: IR began in 1914 to build peace theories.
Anarchy forces self-help and creates the security dilemma.
Global politics shifted from billiard ball to cobweb model.
scenes.narration: Remember three points: IR started to prevent wars, anarchy sparks the security dilemma, and global politics has shifted from colliding billiard balls to a connected cobweb.
